restrictions: Messages of 55 and 63 bytes (the 63-byte one ends in eight zero bytes): one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and the true block length; unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision of two distinct complete messages.

Cancellation, constants, class of Y4, rule A, Lemma N: c66f230d (Jbenisek, co-author tekkac). Three-level construction, per-outer-step table, staged batch with halting budgets: 60f94c5c (Jbenisek). Stage-B premise 0.60 p_B, Lemma C' and the empirical Bernstein decision rule, a 2^39-trial sample of the 098e66f4 configuration: 52bb50ee (Subflatus3). Stage-B budget 0.6001 p_B: 5266c5ce (leech1996). Member values once per outer step: df8bd46d (Th0rgal); lanes: ticket 2bf40fb (tekkac); complement propagation: 8c81a219 (Th0rgal). Jbenisek, tekkac, Th0rgal, Subflatus3 and leech1996 are co-authors. Ours (18a7fc52, d26a3c5f, 2bb5d604, 098e66f4): S8, beta filter (Lemma B), Lemmas D and D', exact S8 count, block accumulator, stage C, a random word per outer step, exact stage values, Chernoff bound on the budgets; new: D3.d1 = X3 (X14 = 0, stage A 28 operations) and a preregistered sample of this configuration. Not used: the sub-class, eight-condition rule, E1 test stage and budget premises of 60f94c5c.

Exact part: for every eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7 (Theorem 1), with Y4 in S8; stage A passes a lane iff its trial satisfies rule A (Lemma A'), stage B iff it satisfies rule A and the beta filter (Lemma F), and stage C computes the XOR differences of digest words 1, 3, 4 and 6 exactly (Lemmas D, D'). With D3.d1 = X3 (so X14 = 0) all of this holds as before (Theorem 1 holds for all eight words). Every good trial (R = 0, rule A, filter) reaches stage C and is found unless a budget has halted the run. Given H1 (ii), each budget is spent with probability below exp(-2.3 * 10^9) (Theorem 2: Chernoff bound over the independent outer steps, for stage C after a union bound inside a batch; no independence inside an outer step, context or batch is used). Heuristic part: N = 1,512,538 * 2^80 = 2^100.53 trials.

256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers; seven trials per word in 36-bit lanes; stage A 28 operations for every batch (C2's d1 = ROR(a1, 16) since X14 = 0), stage B 73 for at most E_B = ceil(0.6001 * p_B * V * 2^64 * 9,363) = 2^94.657 batches (p_B = 0.1992628), stage C 112 for at most E_C = ceil(1.27 * N * 2^-11) = 2^89.873 batches (count-down budget registers; a spent budget halts the run with failure; stages B and C duplicated for each of the 83 unrolled batch positions); with the loop, middle step (107 per X2 value), block test (4), table build (49 per list word) and outer step with its random word (318): 5.3253 operations per trial, every executed primitive including loads, stores and random words counted as 1; no sorting or lookup by value. The time bound holds for every value of the coins. Total 2^94.198131, claimed 94.1982 (holds up to 5.32555 per trial; budget registers in memory 2^94.2124, no unrolling 2^94.3078).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step (V * 2^32 words; three 32-bit words of each are used, vc, S15 and S9; D3.d1 = X3 is fixed). Success probability 0.39 holds only under H1, the only heuristic, with parts (i) and (ii). The factor F = 92,675,072 = 2^26.4657 in H1 (i) is assumed; it is half of an exact model count of 185,350,144 (margin 2.000), recomputed by the shipped program's --count mode, that the organizer experiments do not measure. H1 (ii) asserts, as run averages, 0.60 times the exact model value p_B of the event that a batch enters stage B (the value of 52bb50ee, with the budget 0.6001 p_B of 5266c5ce; it lies below p_B because rule A clusters by context and rests on uniform samples of the run, not on M) and 1.25 times the exact model rate 2^-11 of rule A with the filter. With the uniform rate the same search gives about 120.7. No full collision is exhibited.

Preprocessing: a declared upper-bound charge (not a premise; H1 and the success bound do not use it) of 2^86 units (2^94.75 word operations) covers all selection of the stored constants, class, rule A, sub-class, filter and stage tests and of the order of the construction and the staged batch by c66f230d, 60f94c5c and by us, and of the stage-B premise and budget values by 52bb50ee and 5266c5ce, without reliance on run records (more than 2^34 times c66f230d's own estimate). Memory 2^100 bytes bounds that preprocessing by its charged work; the search itself uses under 2^21 bytes. Advice under 64 bytes.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's random words (one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step, supplying vc, S15 and S9; D3.d1 = X3), (i) the N = 1,512,538 * 2^80 trials of proof.md Section 4 behave, with respect to the event good (128-bit residual R = 0, rule A, and E1's c1 passes the beta filter), like independent events of probability at least F * 2^-128 each (F = 92,675,072 = 185,350,144 / 2 = 2^26.4657), to the extent that the probability that no trial is good is at most exp(-lambda) + 0.002 with lambda = N * F * 2^-128 = 0.4980001; and (ii) averaged over the V * 2^64 * 9,363 batches of the run, the probability that a batch has a trial satisfying rule A is at most 0.60 * p_B, and averaged over the N trials, the probability that a trial satisfies rule A and passes the beta filter is at most 1.25 * 2^-11, where p_B = 32,052,445,611,625 / 160,855,115,169,792 = 0.1992628 and 2^-11 are the exact values of these two stage events under the seven-word model M that gives the count of (i), with the distinct trials of a batch independent as in (i). The stage-B value 0.60 p_B is from 52bb50ee (Subflatus3); it lies below the M value because rule A clusters by context, and it rests on uniform samples of the run, not on M.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Fact P, the construction of Section 2, Y4 in the sub-class S8 of Section 3 (all 65,536 members per outer step and X2, in the stated order, seven per batch, 9,363 batches), the three words vc, S15, S9 from the outer step's own random word and D3.d1 = X3 (so X14 = 0), vd below 1,512,538, w5 and X2 over 2^32 values each; rule A as in Lemma A; the filter (c1 AND 00098188) = 00008000. Part (ii) concerns averages over all batches and all trials of the run, not single contexts or batches.
heuristics.extrapolation: (i) From an exact count under the seven-word model M (proof.md Section 8.1): restricted to the six betas of T6, which the filter contains by Lemma B, the share of solutions of R = 0 with rule A among Y4 in S8 times 2^192 is 185,350,144 * 2^-128, an exact integer from 57 nonzero of 85 outcomes counted by carry automata in exact integer arithmetic without sampling (equal with and without rule A). The shipped program recomputes it: python3 experiments/s8stage.py --count prints N1, N3 and the part of every outcome, the six per-beta parts and the total (about 2 minutes). Our C counter, the Python port and a separately written counter (183,119,872 for the four heaviest betas) agree exactly; a sampling estimator by our review agent gives ratio 1.0007 +- 0.0047; every member of S8 has an exact factor of at least 184.57M (all 15 betas); the full-class parts equal the published table of c66f230d; brute force at 8-bit words agrees on every outcome, member split and rule split. On real trials, rule-A and filter rates agree with the model at rates 2^-5 to 2^-11, the E1 part has real/model 1.0086 over 2^33.8 trials, and E3 partial events of probability about 2^-38 show the counter's S8-versus-rest ratios (1, 2.333, 7) on real trials as on model draws. F is exactly half of the count. (ii) Under M, h1 and c1 are independent uniform words; rule A holds for 2^27 of 2^32 words h1 and the filter for 2^26 of 2^32 words c1, so rule A with the filter has rate exactly 2^-11, and a batch of seven (last batch: two) distinct independent trials has a rule-A trial with probability 1 - (31/32)^7 (1 - (31/32)^2), giving p_B (--count enumerates the patterns and prints these integers and the fraction p_B). The stage-B part is not extrapolated from M: it is a run average estimated by uniform sampling of the run's own index space. A preregistered uniform sample of this configuration (proof.md Section 8.2; 65,536 outer steps with vd, w5, vc, S15, S9 and 16 values of X2 drawn uniformly, D3.d1 = X3, all S8 members, 2^36 trials; its counts equal the shipped program's forward computation and batching on three full drawn contexts) gives, per outer step, a stage-B batch share of 0.53912 +- 0.00022 of p_B (empirical Bernstein bound 0.5493 p_B at delta = 2^-64; by Lemma C', a lower-tail Chernoff bound proved in the text, a run average of 0.60 p_B or more would give a sample this low with probability below exp(-40.3); the preregistered decision rule required both) and a rule-A-and-filter rate of 1.00007 +- 0.00017 of 2^-11 (normal 99.9% bound 1.0006 against 1.25); per run of 8,192 outer steps 0.5386 to 0.5401 and 0.9988 to 1.0013. A control with random D3.d1 (2^34) gives 0.54663 and 1.00076; the earlier uniform samples of the 098e66f4 configuration (098e66f4, 2^38: 0.54629 and 1.00001; 52bb50ee, 2^39, independently written program: 0.54644 and 0.99995) and the 41 replays of this version (0.544 +- 0.007 and 1.003 +- 0.057) agree. The extrapolation is from these samples to the averages over all 2^100.53 trials and 2^97.7 batches of the run.
heuristics.limitations: The factor of (i) is assumed, set at exactly half of a model count that organizer experiments do not measure (margin 2.000). M is untested at probability 2^-100.5; real trials were compared with it for events down to about 2^-38 per trial (E1 part, E3 partial events) and about 2^-40 for one call in c66f230d; the full E3 event has too few hits at our sample size to test (real 0.80 +- 0.20, model draws 0.51 +- 0.15 with the same estimator). M fails inside one context for rule A (clustering); only averages over contexts are measured, and part (ii) and Theorem 2 use only such averages. The clustering makes the real stage-B batch share about 0.54 of p_B on average with D3.d1 = X3 (0.55 with random D3.d1), while single contexts reach 0.95 to 1.13 p_B and single outer steps 0.88 p_B; (ii) bounds only the run average. The constants, class and rule A were chosen by c66f230d to maximize a count of this kind; S8 is the best under M of 8,992,320 sub-classes given by three one- or two-bit conditions on e1 and supplies a factor 1.29 of the margin (if its advantage under M were entirely a selection artifact, S8 trials would have the class rate, and the full class with rule A counts 1.555 F >= F); the filter was chosen to contain the heaviest betas; choices that are best under M may favour parameters where M overstates. 37% of the S8 count (44% in the full class) comes from one beta, 18b0e098. Trials of one outer step share its three coin words (D3.d1 = X3 in all outer steps) and trials of one context differ only in Y4; for (i) their independence is assumed. The deeper real-trial checks of (i) (E1 part, E3 partial events) were made with random D3.d1; with D3.d1 = X3 only rule A, the filter, beta in T6 and the low bits of the Lemma N word were measured again (2^36 trials, rates equal to the random-D3.d1 ones within 0.2%). Part (ii) is estimated from a uniform sample of 2^36 trials of this configuration, not from the 2^100.5 of the run, and only on the participant side with a seeded generator; its stage-B margin over the observed mean is about 1.11 (098e66f4's 1.01 p_B had about 1.85). The value 0.60 was chosen by 52bb50ee after reading 098e66f4's sample and adopted here before our preregistered sample; the budget 0.6001 p_B (5266c5ce) replaced the planned 0.61 p_B after the sample, which changes only the halt point, not the premise or the measured share; the earlier samples (2^38, 2^39) are of the random-D3.d1 configuration, whose share is 0.0075 p_B higher. The [0, 1]-range bounds are not informative for the rare stage-C event; its margin 1.25 is supported by per-outer-step means only. The organizer experiments see the stage events in 16,128 clustered lanes per run. The count program runs on the participant side (about 2 minutes), not as an organizer experiment. Run selection: no organizer-run count or frequency supports F or the averages of (ii); the experiments' predictions are exact per-seed predicates, every recorded replay of this version is reported (proof.md Section 6: 41 participant-run local replays with program, harness and nonces hashed before running), every run of the preregistered sample is reported, and no parameter, version, seed or nonce was chosen on replay or sample outcomes (D3.d1 = X3 was chosen from the operation count).
